audit.whatIsWrong: The page's core defensive plan is to eat Ruthless Predator on Valor's shield, and later on Immortal Shieldbow. The early prose says 'use E defensively first when he dashes in, let the shield eat a hit'; the mid prose says 'dash at him with E to provoke the stun, eat it on the shield'; whys[5] says 'your shield absorbs his W opener'; the late prose says 'your shield absorbs the first hit'. All four are the same instruction.
audit.why: Riot's text for Ruthless Predator at 50+ Fury: 'he slashes his target three times, destroying damage shields on the target, dealing high physical damage, and stunning them for 1.5 seconds.' It removes the shield rather than being absorbed by it - so the exact moment the page tells you to rely on Valor is the moment Valor is worth nothing, and the same applies to the Shieldbow proc the late-game plan is built on. The renekton__riven mirror flagged shield destruction from the other side as the thing his page also failed to state.
audit.corrected: All four fields rewritten to say the empowered stun destroys damage shields, with spacing and anti-heal named as the real answers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Skill, Riven, Riven, Skill, Skill, Riven, Riven while the packet chart over 3221 games reads Skill, Renekton, Renekton, Renekton, Renekton, Renekton, Skill - and Riven's win rate here is 48.31%, the only losing matchup in this slice.
audit.why: The chart gives Riven four stages of a lane she loses, and does it while the page's own prose says the opposite: the early paragraph opens 'Renekton is one of the few melee matchups where you do not own Level 2' on a row marked Riven, and the mid paragraph calls Levels 3 through 5 'his peak ownership window' on rows marked Riven and Skill. The renekton__riven mirror is first-hand and explicit that this direction needs the inverse of its chart, with ratings inverted from 5/7/7/7/7/6/5.
audit.corrected: Rows 1 through 6 flipped as one atomic paired group in both layers to Skill, Renekton, Renekton, Renekton, Renekton, Renekton, Skill, with ratings set to the inverse of the mirror's.

audit.whatIsWrong: The mid prose puts Ruthless Predator on 'a 13-second cooldown', and whys[5], whys[6], the first-item spike and the late prose all claim the matchup flips to Riven once Immortal Shieldbow completes.
audit.why: Ruthless Predator is 16/14/12/10/8s - sixteen at rank 1, not thirteen, and it halves by rank 5, so the safe window shrinks through exactly the levels the page tells you to trade in. And the flip claim does not survive the data: 48.31% over 3221 games means the two-item game is at best even, which is what the corrected chart says. Overstating it tells a player to force a duel the numbers say she does not win.
audit.corrected: Real cooldown range written into whys[2], the Level 2 spike, the early prose, the mid prose and wants.you[0]; the flip language softened to 'evens out' in whys[6], the first-item spike and the late prose so the text agrees with the chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cull the Meek is called 'Cull of the Meek' in the mid prose and in wants.foe[0].
audit.why: The real name in Riot's data is Cull the Meek. Same class of error as the calibration examples, and the packet's suspectNames did not catch it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grievous Wounds is absent from the content layer entirely, though the full layer's Itemization line already calls for Executioner's Calling.
audit.why: Cull the Meek heals him for a portion of the damage dealt and heals more above 50 Fury, on a flat 7-second cooldown - it is the reason his extended trades hold up, and the one thing that turns it off is anti-heal. Ruthless Predator is also an auto reset, so the burst tell is the attack wind-up rather than the cast.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal timing written into the mid prose and the first-item spike; the auto reset written into the Level 2 spike.

edits.after: Renekton stops scaling at two items while you keep climbing, so the 1v1 levels out rather than reversing — and any lead he banked at Levels 2-5 still shows as a tower advantage you have to erase with roams.

edits.after: With Fury stacked he can Slice and Dice in, stun through your shield rather than into it, Cull twice, and dash out — respect that pattern every single trade.

edits.before: Renekton is one of the few melee matchups where you do not own Level 2. His empowered W comes online simultaneously with yours, and his point-click stun interrupts your Q chain mid-animation — if he hits that stun while you are in Q2 or Q3 cast, your whole combo drops and you eat his full rotation for free. At Level 1, poke with Q autos at the tip of range without auto-weaving into his face; he has no escape or stun yet and your Q chip is safe. The moment he hits Level 2, treat every step forward as a potential empowered-W death sentence: use E defensively first when he dashes in, let the shield eat a hit, and disengage rather than extending into his fury window.
edits.after: Renekton is one of the few melee matchups where you do not own Level 2. Ruthless Predator arrives alongside your own stun and point-clicks you out of Broken Wings mid-animation — if it lands during Q2 or Q3 the whole combo drops and you eat his rotation for free. At Level 1, chip with Broken Wings at the tip of its range without auto-weaving into his face; he has no stun yet and that poke is safe. From Level 2, treat every step forward as a potential empowered-W death sentence, and do not plan around Valor absorbing it: above 50 Fury that stun destroys damage shields outright, so disengage instead of extending into his Fury window.

edits.before: Levels 3 through 5 are his peak ownership window. He can E-in, empowered-W stun you through your E shield, Q twice for massive burst, and E-out before your animation recovery finishes — the net damage is heavily in his favour and he heals through Cull of the Meek on top of it. Your only winning trade pattern in this window is to bait the empowered W first: dash at him with E to provoke the stun, eat it on the shield, then immediately chain Q1-Q2-W-Q3 while his stun is a 13-second cooldown. If fury is showing on his bar and you have not seen the empowered W recently, do not step up. Play for CS, track fury, and make him burn it into minions before you trade. At Level 6 his Dominus goes up, but your Wind Slash execute gives you an actual kill threat in short trades he cannot disengage from cleanly — wait for sub-50% HP windows and let R do the work.
edits.after: Levels 3 through 5 are his peak ownership window. He can Slice and Dice in, stun you through Valor because the empowered version destroys damage shields, Cull the Meek twice for the burst, and dash back out before your recovery ends — and he heals off every Cull on top of it. Your only winning pattern is to bait that stun out first: feint with Valor to draw it, then chain Broken Wings and Ki Burst inside its cooldown, which is 16 seconds at rank 1 and only 8 by rank 5. If Fury is showing and you have not seen the stun recently, do not step up. Play for CS and make him spend Fury on minions. Buy Executioner's Calling early — the healing, not the burst, is what wins his long trades. At Level 6 Dominus goes up, but Wind Slash gives you a real kill threat in short trades he cannot leave cleanly.

edits.before: Once you hit Immortal Shieldbow the matchup flips. Renekton does not scale into items — his empowered W still hurts but your shield absorbs the first hit, your healing sustains the second, and your burst at full combo now exceeds his. He becomes a non-threat in side lane at two items while you are still climbing. The real danger past this point is an early death count — if he kills you twice before first back he snowballs into a tower-dive threat at Level 6 with Dominus that the whole structure of your comeback depends on surviving. Keep the game close in gold, survive his spike, and trust that the post-first-item version of this lane belongs to you.
edits.after: Once you hit Immortal Shieldbow the matchup evens out rather than flipping. Renekton does not scale into items, but an empowered Ruthless Predator destroys damage shields, so neither Valor nor the Shieldbow proc answers his opener — spacing and anti-heal do. He stops being the aggressor in side lane at two items while you are still climbing. The real danger past this point is an early death count: if he kills you twice before first back he snowballs into a Level 6 Dominus dive threat your whole comeback depends on surviving. Keep the gold gap tight, survive his spike, and take the even duel rather than forcing a losing one.

edits.after: Bait Ruthless Predator with a Valor feint, then retaliate only inside the 8 to 16 seconds it stays down

edits.before: Stack fury with Cull of the Meek procs before committing his empowered W so the stun duration is maximised
edits.after: Stack Fury with Cull the Meek before committing the stun, so it runs 1.5s and destroys your shield

edits.before: Use E-W-Q-E to trade in and out before your three-hit Q chain can return all the damage

notes: The most costly error in this matchup was a plan, not a name: four separate fields told the player to absorb Ruthless Predator on Valor and later on Immortal Shieldbow, when the empowered version destroys damage shields on the target. Following that advice means spending your only defensive layer at the exact moment it does nothing. 'Cull of the Meek' is a fabricated name (real: Cull the Meek) and the packet's suspectNames missed it, so the name checker has a gap for of-inserted variants. Chart: this is the one losing matchup in the slice at 48.31% over 3221 games, and the page gave Riven four of seven stages; rows 1-6 proposed as one atomic paired group matching the packet and the inverse of the renekton__riven mirror's ratings, and I softened whys[6], the first-item spike and the late prose so the prose no longer claims a flip the chart and the data both deny. DATA DISCREPANCY the mirror also raised: brief header games and packet.games agree here at 3221, unlike mel, ornn, olaf, pantheon and poppy in this slice, where they differ.
